sections.html:
The Treasurer and the Assessment Office share the building at 307 W. Center Street in Cambridge, the county seat. The County Clerk files the levies and extends the tax to each parcel, usually finishing in April, and then the Treasurer prints and mails the bills. The Board of Review has three citizen members named by the County Board chair, and the Chief County Assessor is its clerk.

  • Treasurer: 309-937-3576, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4:30 pm except holidays
  • Assessment Office: 309-937-3570, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4:30 pm
  • Cities: Colona, Galva, Geneseo and Kewanee. Villages include Alpha, Andover, Bishop Hill, Cambridge, Cleveland, Orion and Woodhull.

sections.h2: Henry County housing at a glance
sections.html: Henry County is a mostly agricultural county in northwest Illinois, in the Davenport-Moline-Rock Island metro area, with Kewanee its largest city. Its housing is older and owner-heavy. Population is 48,095, down 2.4% from the 2020 base, with 22,199 housing units and owners in 79.9% of homes. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $151,600. Median gross rent is $842 and median household income is $71,911.

The Assessment Office handles just over 31,000 parcels with a total assessed value of $1,535,199,680. The levy process draws on 124 taxing districts, 23 drainage districts and 27 TIF districts. Districts file their requests on the last Tuesday in December, and the Clerk checks them against the Truth-in-Taxation law and statutory rate limits.

Property is valued as of January 1 each year. For new construction, the statute makes the January 1 owner liable, on a proportionate basis, for the added tax from the date the occupancy permit issued or the improvement became fit for use through December 31. If you finished an addition last year, ask the Assessment Office how that proration affects your next bill.

Henry County bills in two installments. For tax year 2025 payable 2026, the due dates were in June and September. Ask the Treasurer for the dates that apply to the tax year you're closing in, and read the bill itself, since banks can't take payment after the second due date.

Henry County accepts payment by card, e-check, mail, drop box, in person, through local banks and by automatic withdrawal. Cards cost 2.25% plus $1.50 per transaction and e-checks $2, paid to the processor. The courthouse drop box takes everything except cash.

Henry County payment programs and limits
ProgramTerms
Automatic withdrawal (ACH)Debits on the first and second due dates; form must arrive 10 business days before a due date
Pre-paymentsDecember 1 to April 1; must be current on prior taxes; up to the previous year's amount only
Pre-payment methodsNo online payments or credit cards
Local banksEight banks accept bills with the full statement; not after the second due date

With pre-payments, the bill later shows the remaining balance or a refund owed on overages once bills are generated. Money paid in advance can't be pulled back before then.

Unpaid taxes become delinquent, and the Treasurer runs a sale of them every year. Tax buyers, professional and private, bid for the right to buy the delinquent amount, and the winner pays the outstanding tax. You don't lose the house right away. Owners have two and a half years to redeem, after which the buyer may grant an extension or petition the Circuit Court for a tax deed.

  • Original interest on a sold tax can run from 0% to 18% annually, plus court costs, certified mailing and other fees.
  • Redemption goes through the County Clerk. Bring the parcel number, because the amount owed depends on the day.
  • Redemption must be paid in full by cash, money order or bank cashier's check. Illinois law doesn't allow personal checks or credit cards for it.

If you're selling a house whose taxes were sold, ask the Clerk for the redemption figure early.

sections.h2: Assessment appeals and the senior freeze
sections.html:
The Chief County Assessor equalizes values and publishes changes between October 15 and November 15 each year. The Board of Review accepts appeals for 30 days after publication. If the Board's written decision doesn't satisfy you, you have 30 days from the date of that notice to go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board. Splits and combinations of parcels must be requested by September 30.

Get the Board of Review complaint form from the Assessment Office. The Board checks whether the township assessor and county assessor calculated values correctly. It can equalize assessments, add omitted property, rule on homestead exemptions and review non-homestead exemption applications.

  • The senior freeze income limit rose from $65,000 to $75,000. An owner with income at or under $75,000 who has never qualified can file the form on the county site or call the office.
  • Freeze forms are mailed each January to everyone who qualified the year before.
  • Ask the Assessment Office for the residential exemption applications.

sections.h2: Selling with tax due at closing
sections.html:
Here is the order that keeps a Henry County closing on track:

  • Open the county's Property Tax Inquiry site with the parcel number and read the bill and payment status.
  • Phone the Treasurer at 309-937-3576 for a payoff figure through the planned closing date, and ask which installments are still open for the year of closing.
  • Call the Clerk if any year was sold at the delinquent sale.
  • Get every payoff in writing for the title company.

Pre-payments are worth knowing about if you list in winter or spring. The program lets a current-on-taxes owner send money ahead of the bills, and the remaining balance or any refund shows up once the new bills are generated. Tell the title company about any pre-payment so the closing statement credits it correctly. If the buyer will take over an automatic withdrawal, remember the form has to reach the Treasurer 10 business days before a due date, so the new owner should file their own.

With a countywide median value of $151,600, an old tax debt or a repair bill is a heavy share of what many houses here are worth. Selling as is to a cash buyer is one way to skip repairs and settle the tax in the purchase contract, as long as the payoffs are confirmed in writing first.

faqs.q: When are Henry County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two installments. For tax year 2025 payable 2026, they were due in June and September. The Treasurer posts the dates for each year on the Treasurer page of the county website.

faqs.q: Can a Henry County bank take my property tax after the second due date?
faqs.a: No. Banks can't accept payments after the second due date. After that, the Treasurer's office is where you pay, and a delinquent bill can go to the annual sale.

faqs.q: How long can a Henry County owner redeem sold taxes?
faqs.a: Two and a half years. After that the tax buyer may extend the time or petition the Circuit Court for a tax deed. Redemption goes through the County Clerk in cash, money order or cashier's check only.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Henry County assessment?
faqs.a: Thirty days after assessments are published, which happens between October 15 and November 15. A further appeal to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board must be filed within 30 days of the Board of Review's written decision.

faqs.q: Does Henry County offer a way to pay property tax early?
faqs.a: Yes, a pre-payment program runs from December 1 to April 1. You must be current on prior-year taxes and may pay up to the previous year's amount only. A form is filled out each year at the time of payment.
